finding: 1. Deadline starts when the world is made, a few ms after import
evidence: Still true on main: realWorld() sets endsAt = Date.now()+20_000 (trace.mjs:842), and hook.mjs:68 makes the world after reading stdin and readsOf. Since 1b5e73e/ab30793 (#37/#34), the archive block also draws on world.timeLeft, so nothing important runs outside the budget. The 10s gap to the 30s hook timeout absorbs the few ms. No later issue or fix touches it.

finding: 2. ~220-line closure factory; a context object would avoid the re-indent
evidence: A style point. realWorld() is still a closure factory on main (trace.mjs:841-1071). #34/PR #38 built on it (timeLeft added to the world) without trouble, and no later issue arose. The PR #35 body gives the reason: git diff -w stays at 35 lines.

finding: 3. engines >=20.11 is only advisory; the test fails on older Node
evidence: Factually true: npm only warns about engines. But the repo has no CI, everything runs on Node 24, and nothing in later history failed on an old Node. package.json still says >=20.11.

finding: 4. No-op reads literal duplicated in the test and realWorld
evidence: Low severity, but the author acted on it later. #37 added a third copy (archive.test). The #34 round-1 Standards review flagged 'the repeated reads stub' again, and 756657a extracted it to test/helpers.mjs noReads(). Only the test copies were merged: realWorld keeps its own literal (trace.mjs:1071).

finding: 5. ADR 0006 'applies only in opted-in repositories' is now contradicted
evidence: In #34's round-1 comment the author said 'ADR 0006 is left unchanged'. The human's halt decision then explicitly 'replaces ... the round-1 decision to leave ADR 0006 unchanged' and requires that it 'qualifies applies only in opted-in repositories'. a8fd424 and later commits amended it: 'Whether a repository is opted in is itself git's answer, so the halt reaches any repository ...'. Related bug B18 (82f120f): read-only commands were refused in untraced repos.

finding: 6. Narrowings left for the human: PostToolUse never halts; over-long history command denied not halted; unparseable gh output keeps bypass; any prompt lifts halt; crashed/killed hook cannot halt
evidence: The reviewer was right that each one departs from the human's halt criteria ('whenever any hook ... halts'). The departures are documented in ADR 0006 and the README and were listed under 'For the human to confirm'. The human merged PR #38 on 2026-10-30T17:30Z without objecting, and there is no later issue. A crashed or killed hook cannot halt at all, so that one is a platform limit.

finding: 7. ADR 0005/0006 still name to-tickets/implement
evidence: Still the case after four more amendments to ADR 0006 in #34: it says 'tickets come from to-tickets', and ADR 0005's table names to-spec/to-tickets/implement. The author's answer (the ADRs record what is reused, and the human runs those skills) holds: SKILL.md and TRACK_HINT now route the model to gh issue create. No later bug came from the ADR wording.

finding: 8. Band counts Review done on any open PR
evidence: ADR 0006 step 5 defines Review as 'a PR whose body says Closes #<n>', and status.mjs:105 follows it ('only an open PR does it'). #31 scoped this out on purpose. It is pre-existing design, not a defect, and no later issue.

finding: 9. Two Track refusals stay as duplicate literals
evidence: Round 2 answered 'stay as literals'. Round 3 (fd98d53) moved both into one TRACK_HINT constant to fix this duplication, and the round-4 comment records the reversal ('This also corrects round 2's refusals stay literals'). TRACK_HINT is on main at trace.mjs:24.

finding: 10. Round 2 dropped ADR 0007's applies-to narrowing (overcorrection)
evidence: The claim was accurate: d4dac3b said 'every active ADR'. It was fixed in fd98d53, and that restatement then drifted, giving 7 of the 8 round-3 findings. The merged 152cded goes back to 'every active ADR' on purpose ('Reading every ADR always satisfies the gates, and the hooks narrow the set themselves'). Over-reading is harmless, and acting on the finding cost rounds. This is the contested B16b: not a bug.

finding: 11. Review base not named (default branch or blocker's)
evidence: fd98d53 added '(the default branch, or the blocker's branch while stacked)' to both SKILL.md and the band. dd26dbe removed only the band copy, which was wrong for a PR merged into the blocker's branch. The SKILL.md copy survived the merge and is still on main (SKILL.md:16). The content was right; only putting it in the band was wrong.

finding: 12. LGTM (no findings) on PR #24
evidence: PR #24 (46490e1) put both /plugin commands in one code block, and pasting it fails ('... is not a valid GitHub owner/repo shorthand'). This was filed as #27 and fixed in 772cbef (PR #28). The LGTM missed a real bug.

finding: 13. Re-nudge after a rebase or with a fast clock; /clear keeping reads
evidence: Re-nudging on a new pushed head is the specified behaviour ('asks once per pushed head'). For /clear, vendor/claude-code/index.d.ts:11713 says a /clear continues 'under a new session id', so session-keyed reads do not carry over; hook.mjs only needs to clear reads on compaction (line 41). No later issue or fix.

finding: 14. rsync --remove-sent-files; recording the #7 decision in code
evidence: The verifier's refutation was wrong for the rsync half, and I reproduced the bypass in this adjudication. On this machine's /usr/bin/rsync (openrsync, 2.6.9-compatible), `rsync -r --remove-sent-files a/ b/` and the abbreviation `--remove-so` both delete the source files, exit 0. guard() returns null for both, because guard.mjs:125 checks c.args.includes('--remove-source-files') exactly. The rule came in with PR #21 (b418246). It is unfixed on main, and no issue has been filed. The '#7 decision in code' half stays refuted.

finding: 15. ADR 0005 still mentions quality-loop
evidence: ADR 0005 is the decision to replace quality-loop, so naming it (and the quality-loop-v0.1.0 tag) is the historical record. It is unchanged on main, with no later issue.

finding: 16. Spec flagged TStack precedence rule, to-spec/implement as skills to use, guard rm -r coverage
evidence: Mixed. The to-spec/implement part was right: the PR #12 rebuttal ('installed skills') was wrong, because #31 showed to-tickets, to-spec and implement set disable-model-invocation, so the model's Skill call fails (B6/B12, fixed in 195172b). The TStack rule came from the request, and the guard does cover rm -r, so those two parts stay wrong.

finding: 17. ADR 0005 still names quality-loop
evidence: Duplicate of #15: waived as the decision's history and its tag. No later change or issue.

finding: 18. Routes text reading cannot see: scripts, gh api/curl PRs, revert/merge messages, xargs, >> appends, markdown subtleties, piped shell text
evidence: The routes are real. PR #21 closed piped shell text, and the rest are left open on purpose as the seatbelt-not-sandbox limit (ADR 0007; #13 progress comment). No later issue escalated any of them.

finding: 19. Re-nudging after a rebase or with a fast clock; /clear keeping reads
evidence: Duplicate of #13. A new pushed head re-asks by spec. /clear starts a new session id (index.d.ts:11713), so reads do not survive it.

finding: 20. rsync --remove-sent-files; recording the #7 decision in code
evidence: Duplicate of #14. Reproduced: openrsync's --remove-sent-files and --remove-so delete the sources, and guard() returns null (guard.mjs:125 matches only the exact '--remove-source-files'). The guard bypass is still open on main.

finding: 22. ADRs 0005/0006 still name to-tickets/implement; band counts Review done on any open PR; band Review reason lacks standards; Track refusals as literals; guard tests cwd
evidence: This aggregates #7, #8, #9 and #31. finding: 26. ~220-line closure factory re-indents adapters; engines >=20.11 only advisory
evidence: Duplicate of #2 and #3. The factory is still on main and #34 extended it without trouble. Advisory engines never mattered: no CI, Node 24.

evidence: Duplicate of #7. The ADRs are unchanged on main, and the model-facing routes (SKILL.md, TRACK_HINT, status.mjs) were fixed in 195172b. No later bug came from the ADR text.
